response.query: How will cryo‑EM/X‑ray structural data be translated into ProTide redesign decisions, and which mechanism‑based benchmarks (binding pose, incorporation kinetics changes) will trigger chemistry changes?
response.answer: Cryo-EM/X-ray structural data guide ProTide redesign by identifying binding poses and kinetics changes, triggering chemistry modifications for better binding affinity. Benchmarks like improved predicted affinity trigger these changes.

results.content: The crystal structure of this design in complex with HDAC2 revealed two distinct binding modes and peptide conformations in the three protein chains of the asymmetric unit, suggesting flexibility of the peptide as well as presence of iso-energetic binding conformations (Supplementary Fig. 2a). Finally, since in the des1.1.0 crystal structure, the peptide interacts with two water molecules at the pocket of HDAC2, also present in a majority of HDAC2 crystal structures (Supplementary Fig. 4b), and displacing such tightly bound water is likely energetically unfavorable36."), we decided to explicitly include them in the design calculations and bias backbone sampling to start from conformations that interact with structured waters at the HDAC2 interface (Fig. 3b). In the des1.1.0:HDAC2 co-crystal structure, the dominant binding mode in the crystal (chains B and C) has considerably better predicted affinity than the original design model with the same peptide structure (Supplementary Table 7, Fig. 5a).
